title: Integration testing, observability, reconciliation, security, and incident diagnosis

objectives: Test integrations with mocks, sandbox contracts, and synthetic LAB_ data—not production tokens.
Observe HTTP statuses, Limits Remaining, event Replay lag, and logs without printing secrets.
Reconcile using documented keys (Salesforce Id vs remote surrogate) from Integration Patterns state management.
Diagnose incidents by layer: auth (INT-004), contract (INT-005), style (INT-003), then remote vs Salesforce.
diagnostic_question: Prod integration drifted 200 extra ERP invoices, Remaining API is low, and a callout test only passed in production. What tests, signals, reconciliation keys, and security mistakes do you name first?
definition: Operating Salesforce integrations means proving them with tests, watching them with observability, aligning copies with reconciliation, keeping tokens and payloads safe, and diagnosing incidents by contract—not by guesswork. Apex callouts are tested with HttpCalloutMock. REST Limits and status codes are the live signals. Integration Patterns stress keys for state tracking. ([Apex callouts](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_callouts.htm); [Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/dome_limits.htm); [Error codes](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/errorcodes.htm); [Integration Patterns](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/fundamentals/guide/integration-patterns))
why_it_matters: Untested callouts, silent drift, and tokens in logs are how integrations become incidents. Interviewers want a diagnosis order and a key strategy, not 'check the server'.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a flight recorder plus a warehouse cycle count. Tests are simulator flights with fake radios (mocks). Observability is the black box: statuses, Remaining quota, replay lag—never the passenger passport numbers (tokens). Reconciliation is counting crates with agreed serials (keys). Security is locking the cockpit. Incident diagnosis reads the recorder in layers: badge, packing list, flight plan, then the other airport.
deeper_explanation: Testing: HttpCalloutMock / Test.setMock for Apex (INT-006). Contract tests in sandbox against LAB_ data. Do not use SeeAllData production. Event subscribers need idempotency tests (INT-008). Connect tests need a lab OData or a documented limitation if unlicensed (INT-009).

Observability: log HTTP status and errorCode, not Authorization headers (INT-005). GET /limits Remaining. For events, monitor time-to-72-hour cliff (INT-007). Debug logs and Event Monitoring exist; SKU/fields Needs verification—do not invent event types.

Reconciliation: Integration Patterns state-management sidebars: Salesforce stores the remote key, or the remote stores the Salesforce Id (or another surrogate). Drift jobs compare those keys. Virtualization paths have nothing to reconcile unless you also copied (INT-009).

Security: named credentials, least scopes, no tokens in git/logs, inbound connected apps reviewed. Incident order: 401 auth, 400 contract, 403 limits, then remote vs Salesforce clocks/keys, then style mismatch (sync vs batch).

mental_model.analogy: Flight recorder plus warehouse cycle count: mocks are simulators, black box is observability, serial counts are reconciliation, cockpit locks are security, layered readout is diagnosis.
useful_mapping: External Id / Salesforce Id → crate serials
token in log → passport left in the aisle
diagnosis order → badge, packing list, flight plan, other airport
where_it_breaks: Not a full APM product catalog.
Cycle count does not apply to pure virtualization.

teach_back_prompt: Walk a drifted-invoice incident through testing gaps, observability signals, reconciliation keys, security, and diagnosis order.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: I test with mocks and sandbox LAB_ data. I watch status, Remaining, and replay lag—never tokens. I reconcile on agreed keys. I diagnose 401 then 400 then 403 then drift then style.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: Production-only tests are a security and reliability fail. Virtualization has no row cycle count unless we also copied. Idempotency tests belong with INT-008. I will not invent Event Monitoring fields. Named credentials stay the secret store.

terminology.plain: Prove the envelope and contract without burning production.
terminology.precise: Automated mocks (HttpCalloutMock), sandbox contract tests, synthetic LAB_ records; no production tokens.
terminology.non_example: SeeAllData live customer callout as the only test.
terminology.boundary: Vendor contract tests optional and still non-prod.

terminology.plain: The black box: what you can see while it flies.
terminology.precise: HTTP status/errorCode, Limits Remaining, job states, Replay lag, debug logs—without secrets.

terminology.plain: Cycle count with agreed serial numbers.
terminology.precise: Compare Salesforce and remote using stored keys (remote key in Salesforce or Salesforce Id in remote) as Integration Patterns describe.
terminology.example: Nightly count of Invoice External Id vs ERP.
terminology.non_example: Virtualization-only path with no copy and no keys to count.

terminology.plain: Lock tokens, scopes, logs, and inbound apps.
terminology.precise: Named/external credentials, least OAuth scopes, no secrets in source/logs, connected-app review (INT-004).
terminology.confusable_neighbor: OWD/sharing (SEC track) which still applies to data exposed.

terminology.plain: Read the recorder in layers instead of rebooting Salesforce.
terminology.precise: Order: auth 401, contract 400, limits 403, then key drift, then pattern/style mismatch, then remote outage.
terminology.example: 401 after secret rotation before blaming JSON.
terminology.non_example: Only 'network is slow' with no status code.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Apex exception in a trigger unrelated to HTTP.

terminology.plain: Fake rows named so they never look like customers.
terminology.precise: Handbook convention: LAB_ objects/fields in disposable orgs.
terminology.non_example: Cloned production named accounts in a public git fixture.

terminology.precise: Either Salesforce stores remote unique/surrogate key, or remote stores Salesforce Id/other surrogate.

terminology.plain: Counts or fields no longer match.
terminology.precise: Copy-based integrations diverge without reconcile jobs; virtualization drift is usually filter/permission/outage, not a stale store.
terminology.example: 200 extra ERP invoices not in Salesforce.
terminology.non_example: Connect __x empty because ERP is down (not copy drift).

when_to_use: When you must design integration testing, observability, reconciliation, security, and incident diagnosis for a Salesforce interface.
When copies can drift and keys from Integration Patterns must be compared.
When an incident needs a layered 401/400/403 diagnosis instead of guesswork.
When tests still call production or logs still print tokens.
When Remaining API or replay lag is the missing signal.
when_not_to_use: Do not treat this as Event Monitoring SKU documentation—Needs verification.
Do not reconcile a pure Connect virtualization path as if rows were stored.
Do not run production-only tests as the quality gate.
Do not invent allocation numbers while reading Remaining.

worked_example.scenario: Sandbox-to-ERP invoice integration created duplicates in a rehearsal and later would have used a production token in a test. Remaining dropped. Counts drifted by 200.

interview_questions.question: How do you cover testing, observability, reconciliation, security, and incident diagnosis?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Mocks and sandbox LAB_ tests. Watch status, Remaining, replay lag—never tokens. Reconcile copies on keys. Diagnose 401/400/403 then drift then style.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Virtualization is not a cycle count. Event Monitoring fields I will not invent. Named credentials stay the secret store. Patterns require error handling, not silent drop.

interview_questions.question: What is your incident diagnosis order?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: 401 auth, 400 contract, 403 limits, then key drift, then pattern mismatch, then remote outage.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I want a timestamped status code before opinions. I will not reboot Salesforce as step one. Connect emptiness is not copy drift.
interview_questions.example: Failed POST then a later count mismatch.

interview_questions.question: CI used a production refresh token to 'make tests real'.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Revoke token, rotate, move to mocks, treat as a security incident.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: That is an INT-004 token-safety incident. Apex tests must use HttpCalloutMock, not a production refresh token in CI. I add a secret scan for Bearer strings, rotate the leaked credential, and I do not keep the production token as a backup in the pipeline.
interview_questions.example: GitHub secret scan finds a production refresh token inside an Apex HttpCallout test class.

interview_questions.question: Finance says Salesforce is missing 200 ERP invoices.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: If we copy: reconcile External Id, check 403/retries/DLQ. If we only virtualize: we never stored them—look at filters and ERP.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I reconcile on the documented external key from the integration pattern, not on Name. Two hundred missing invoices may be sharing, an ignored done=false page, or HTTP 403 drops. I separate Remaining quota from true key mismatch before I accuse Salesforce of deleting rows.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Invoice__c ExtKey__c versus the ERP invoice list shows 200 keys present only on ERP.

interview_questions.question: Logs are huge and still useless.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: They probably logged payloads/tokens and not status/errorCode/Remaining.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I redraft logging: status, errorCode, correlation id, key—not Bearer. I sample, I do not print every JSON body with PII.
interview_questions.example: Debug log full of Authorization headers.

interview_questions.question: Tests green, production 400s.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Mock body drifted from the vendor contract. Add a sandbox contract test; still no production tokens.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Green tests with production HTTP 400s usually mean the mock drifted from the vendor JSON/XML contract (INT-005). I update the mock after change control and add observability on 400 rate. A required field the vendor added will pass an old 200 mock and fail live.
interview_questions.example: Vendor added a required JSON field; sandbox mock still returns 200 with the old body.

interview_questions.question: What do you monitor on an event-driven integration?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Replay lag versus 72 hours, error handler DLQ, subscriber heartbeat—not SOQL nextRecordsUrl.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: INT-007 retention cliff is the unique signal. I will not invent Event Monitoring names. Idempotency metrics catch duplicates.
interview_questions.example: CDC cache subscriber lag, last Replay ID age, and a dead-letter count on failed handlers.

interview_questions.question: Teach flight-recorder plus cycle-count analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Mocks are simulators, black box is status/Remaining, serials are keys, cockpit locks are credentials. It breaks for virtualization (no crates) and invented APM SKUs.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The flight recorder is status codes, Limits Remaining, and Replay IDs; the cycle count is reconciliation on business keys. It breaks if I treat virtualization as a copy to count, or if I invent OAuth grant bodies while diagnosing. I walk 401, then 400, then 403, then keys, then style.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard HTTP 401 on the callout, then 200 invoices missing after a weekend batch.
